newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden Centre Party head Johansson not resigning.
newsitem.headline: Sweden Centre Party head Johansson not resigning.

text.p: The leader of Sweden's Centre Party, Olof Johansson said on Thursday that he was not resigning from the party leadership despite recent heavy criticism for flagging support in the opinion polls.
"I have decided to stand for re-election (at the party congress this summer)," Johansson told a press conference.
"That is what I have told the election nominating committee today."
The Centre Party has an informal alliance with Sweden's minority Social Democratic government.
Markets were concerned that if Johansson resigned, he could be replaced by a more conservative leader, ending the relationship with the Social Democrats who could then shift more towards the left.
The Centre Party's support in opinion polls have slumped this year.
At the last general election in September 1994 the Centre Party secured 7.7 percent of the vote, the third largest party in the seven party parliament.
But a poll in late March showed the party's support was now below six percent, falling 1.7 percentage points since January this year.
The Centre Party has formed an informal cooperation with the ruling centre-left Social Democrats in the seven party Swedish parliament.

Earlier this year the Social Democrats, Centre and Left parties joined forces on a new energy agreement that will see the closure of one of Sweden's 12 nuclear reactors next year and a second closure in 2001.
Johansson has been leader of the Centre Party for 10 years and at 59 is the oldest of all Sweden's political party leaders.
